title: Give dispatch and support their own deadlines

blocks.text: The shop computes two deadlines from a date. Operations promises customers a ship date, and support promises a reply date for every ticket. Both have called `WorkingDays.add` since someone noticed the two loops were the same; it has since gained a `saturdays` parameter for the warehouse and a `holidays` parameter for support.
This week brings one request from each team:

items: **Operations:** the warehouse now works public holidays, as well as Monday to Saturday. An order ships at most two warehouse days after the day it was placed.

**Support:** nothing changes about which days support works (Monday to Friday, never a public holiday), but a ticket opened on a day support doesn't work now counts as opened on support's next working day. The reply is due one support day after that.

blocks.text: Write `shipBy` and `replyBy` in `src/main/java/practice/Deadlines.java` so that each team gets its request, and neither team's dates move because of the other's. About twelve lines in total.

cases.says: in an ordinary week an order ships two days after it was placed
in an ordinary week a reply is due the day after the ticket was opened
the warehouse counts a public holiday as a working day, while support still doesn't
the warehouse counts Saturday as a working day, while support doesn't
support's new rule for tickets opened on a day off does not move ship dates
a ticket opened on a day support doesn't work counts from support's next working day
the warehouse's new holiday rule does not make support count public holidays
the warehouse's Saturdays do not make support count Saturdays

origin.section: Inlining the Method Back Gives Each Format Its Own Code, and All Checks Pass

concepts: Inlining the method back, copying its body into each caller, substituting that caller's arguments and deleting what can no longer run, gives each owner code the other's change cannot reach.
Code that looks alike but encodes two owners' rules, once merged, lets a change made for one caller break the other.
